q: How did Paul become an apostle of Christ Jesus?
a: Paul became an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God.

q: To whom did Paul write this letter?
a: Paul wrote to those set apart for God and the faithful brothers at Colossae.

q: From where did the Colossians hear about the confident expectation that they now have?
a: The Colossians heard about their confident expectation in the word of truth, the gospel.

q: What does Paul say the gospel has been doing in the world?
a: Paul says the gospel has been bearing fruit and growing in all the world.

q: Who presented the gospel to the Colossians?
a: Epaphras, the faithful servant of Christ, presented the gospel to the Colossians.

q: With what does Paul pray that the Colossians be filled?
a: Paul prays that the Colossians be filled with the knowledge of God’s will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding.

q: How does Paul pray that the Colossians will walk in their lives?
a: Paul prays that the Colossians will walk worthy of the Lord, bearing fruit with good deeds, growing in the knowledge of God.

q: For what have those set apart for God been qualified?
a: Those set apart for God have been qualified for a share in the inheritance in the light.

q: From what has the Father rescued those set apart for him?
a: He rescued them from the dominion of darkness and transferred them to the kingdom of his Son.

q: In Christ, we have redemption, which is what?
a: In Christ we have redemption, which is the forgiveness of sins.

q: The Son is the image of whom?
a: The Son is the image of the invisible God.

q: What was created through Jesus Christ and for him?
a: All things were created through Jesus Christ and for him.

q: How did God reconcile all things to himself?
a: God reconciled all things to himself when he made peace through his Son’s blood.

q: What relationship did the Colossians have with God before they believed the gospel?
a: Before believing the gospel, the Colossians were separated from God and were his enemies.

q: What must the Colossians continue to do?
a: The Colossians must continue to be settled in the faith and confident of the gospel.

q: For whose sake is Paul suffering, and what is his attitude?
a: Paul is suffering for the sake of the church, and he rejoices in it.

q: What is the mystery that was hidden for ages but now has been revealed?
a: The mystery that was hidden for ages but now has been revealed is Christ in you, the confidence of glory.

q: What is the goal for which Paul is admonishing and teaching every man?
a: Paul’s goal is to present every person complete in Christ.

q: What is the mystery of God?
a: The mystery of God is Christ.

q: What is hidden in Christ?
a: All the hidden treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Christ.

q: What is Paul concerned that might happen to the Colossians?
a: Paul is concerned that the Colossians might be deceived with persuasive speech.

q: What does Paul call the Colossians to do now that they have received Christ Jesus?
a: Paul calls the Colossians to walk in Christ Jesus in the same way that they received him.

q: Upon what are the empty deceits that Paul is concerned about based?
a: The empty deceits are based upon human tradition and the sinful belief systems of the world.

q: What lives in Christ?
a: All the fullness of God’s nature lives in Christ.

q: Who is the head of all rule and authority?
a: Christ is the head of all rule and authority.

q: What is removed through the circumcision of Christ?
a: The sinful body of flesh is removed through the circumcision of Christ.

q: What happens in baptism?
a: A person is buried with Christ in baptism.

q: What is a person’s condition before Christ makes him alive?
a: A person is dead in his sins before Christ makes him alive.

q: What did Christ do with the record of debts charged against us?
a: Christ removed the record of debts and nailed it to the cross.

q: What did Christ do with the rulers and authorities?
a: Christ removed the rulers and authorities, openly exposed them, and led them as his captives in a victory procession.

q: What does Paul say are a shadow of the things to come?
a: Paul says that food, drink, feast days, and Sabbaths are a shadow of the things to come.

q: To what reality do the shadows point?
a: The shadows point to the reality of Christ.

q: From what does the whole body grow with the growth from God?
a: The whole body holds fast to Christ, the head, to grow with the growth from God.

q: What kinds of commandments does Paul say are part of the world’s beliefs?
a: Commandments to not handle, not taste, and not touch are part of the world’s beliefs.

q: Against what do the rules of man-made religion have no value?
a: The rules of man-made religion have no value against the indulgence of the flesh.

q: What should believers seek, and what should they not seek?
a: Believers should seek the things above and not the things of the earth.

q: To where has Christ been raised?
a: Christ has been raised to sit at the right hand of God.

q: Where has God put the believer’s life?
a: God has hidden the believer’s life in Christ.

q: What will happen to the believer when Christ is revealed?
a: When Christ is revealed, the believer will also be revealed with him in glory.

q: What must the believer put to death?
a: The believer must put to death the sinful desires of the earth.

q: What happens to those who are disobedient to God?
a: The wrath of God comes upon those who are disobedient to God.

q: What are some of the things that Paul says the believers must get rid of, which are part of the old self?
a: The believers must get rid of wrath, anger, evil intentions, insults, and obscene speech.

q: In whose image is the believer’s new self created?
a: The believer’s new self is created in the image of Christ.

q: What are some of the things that Paul says the believers must put on, which are part of the new self?
a: The believers must put on a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, meekness, and patience.

q: In what way should the believer forgive?
a: The believer should forgive in the same way that the Lord has forgiven him.

q: What is the bond of perfection among believers?
a: Love is the bond of perfection.

q: What should the believer give to God in his attitude, song, word, and deed?
a: In his attitude, song, word, and deed, the believer should give thanks to God.

q: What should rule in the believer’s heart?
a: The peace of Christ should rule in the believer’s heart.

q: What should live in the believer richly?
a: The word of Christ should live in the believer richly.

q: How should a wife respond to her husband?
a: A wife should submit to her husband.

q: How should a husband treat his wife?
a: A husband should love his wife and not be bitter against her.

q: How should a child treat his parents?
a: A child should obey his parents in all things.

q: What should a father not do to his children?
a: A father should not provoke his children.

q: For whom are believers working in whatever they do?
a: Believers are working for the Lord in whatever they do.

q: What will those receive who serve the Lord in whatever they do?
a: Those who serve the Lord in whatever they do will receive the reward of the inheritance.

q: What will those receive who do unrighteousness?
a: Those who do unrighteousness will receive the penalty for what they did.

q: What does Paul remind earthly masters that they also have?
a: Paul reminds earthly masters that they also have a master in heaven.

q: In what does Paul want the Colossians to continue steadfastly?
a: Paul wants the Colossians to continue steadfastly in prayer.

q: For what does Paul want the Colossians to pray?
a: Paul wants the Colossians to pray that he has an open door to speak the word, the mystery of Christ.

q: How does Paul instruct the Colossians to treat those who are outsiders?
a: Paul instructs them to live in wisdom, and speak with grace toward those who are outsiders.

q: What task had Paul given Tychicus and Onesimus?
a: Paul gave them the task of making everything known concerning him to the Colossians.

q: What instructions did Paul give concerning Mark, the cousin of Barnabas?
a: Paul told the Colossians to receive Mark if he comes to them.

q: For what does Epaphras pray for the Colossians?
a: He prays that the Colossians will stand complete and fully assured in all the will of God.

q: What is the name of the physician that is with Paul?
a: The physician’s name is Luke.

q: In what kind of place was the church in Laodicea meeting?
a: The church in Laodicea was meeting in a house.

q: To what other church had Paul also written a letter?
a: Paul also had written a letter to the church in Laodicea.

q: How did Paul show that this letter was actually from him?
a: Paul wrote his name in his own handwriting at the end of the letter.
